question.:question/problem: Calculate the instantaneous rate of change of the function $f(x)=-4tan⁡x$ when $x=\pi .$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The instantaneous rate of change  when $x=\pi$ is given by the value of the derivative ${f}^{′}(x)$ at $x=\pi .$ 

First, we compute the derivative, using the fact that $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(tan⁡x)={sec}^{2}⁡x.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-4tan⁡x) \\  & =-4{sec}^{2}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=\pi ,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\pi ) & =-4{sec}^{2}⁡\pi  \\  & =-4\cdot (-1)^{2} \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,  the instantaneous rate of change is $-4.$
